# Controller REST reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_api_docs.py from meshforge.controller.http.openapi_document(). DO NOT EDIT. -->

API: **MeshForge controller**, version `0.17.0`, OpenAPI 3.1.0.

The compute fabric's REST surface. Every call but /healthz and POST /v1/auth/login needs a user's API token (`compute login`).

75 operations.

### `GET /healthz`

Healthz

Liveness probe: the process is up; ``sessions`` = live agent streams.
``"degraded"`` (still 200) names a supervised background loop that keeps
failing (V0.7 G5, D159 N4: the stream auth re-check).

|---|---|---|

| 400 | Invalid input (`invalid_input`) | `application/json` [ErrorEnvelope](#schema-errorenvelope) |
| 401 | No, or no longer a valid, credential (`unauthorized`) | `application/json` [ErrorEnvelope](#schema-errorenvelope) |
| 403 | Not allowed: admin only, CSRF, foreign origin (`unauthorized`) | `application/json` [ErrorEnvelope](#schema-errorenvelope) |
| 404 | Not found - also another user's object (`not_found`) | `application/json` [ErrorEnvelope](#schema-errorenvelope) |

### `GET /v1/nodes`

Every known node

All enrolled nodes with their live state (D16: three separate fields).

The table holds one row per node that ever enrolled, not one per event, so
``limit`` exists to keep the promise that *every* list endpoint is bounded
rather than to page through a large result. There is deliberately no offset or
cursor yet (a V0.8 conversation): ``count`` is the number of rows returned, and
no ``total`` is served because counting every node would mean a second query on
a path an operator polls with ``--watch``.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `limit` | query | integer | no | Nodes returned, by node_id. (minimum 1, maximum 5000, default `500`) |

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | Successful Response | `application/json` [NodeList](#schema-nodelist) |
| 400 | Invalid input (`invalid_input`) | `application/json` [ErrorEnvelope](#schema-errorenvelope) |
| 401 | No, or no longer a valid, credential (`unauthorized`) | `application/json` [ErrorEnvelope](#schema-errorenvelope) |
| 403 | Not allowed: admin only, CSRF, foreign origin (`unauthorized`) | `application/json` [ErrorEnvelope](#schema-errorenvelope) |

### `GET /v1/nodes/{node_id}/resources`

One node's resource history and newest live samples

1-minute downsampled history from the database plus the in-memory ring.

The two differ on purpose: history is complete and durable but at most one
minute of resolution, the ring is 2-second resolution and only the last few
minutes of *this* controller process.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `node_id` | path | string | yes | maxLength 32 |
| `since` | query | string (date-time) (nullable) | no | Inclusive lower bound on bucket_start (ISO-8601, UTC). |
| `until` | query | string (date-time) (nullable) | no | Exclusive upper bound on bucket_start (ISO-8601, UTC). |
| `limit` | query | integer | no | History rows. (minimum 1, maximum 10080, default `240`) |
| `live_limit` | query | integer | no | Newest live samples. (minimum 0, maximum 1000, default `30`) |

| Status | Meaning | Body |

| 400 | Invalid input (`invalid_input`) | `application/json` [ErrorEnvelope](#schema-errorenvelope) |
| 401 | No, or no longer a valid, credential (`unauthorized`) | `application/json` [ErrorEnvelope](#schema-errorenvelope) |
| 403 | Not allowed: admin only, CSRF, foreign origin (`unauthorized`) | `application/json` [ErrorEnvelope](#schema-errorenvelope) |

### `GET /v1/nodes/{node_id}/metrics`

One node's live metrics for sparklines (in-memory, last 5 minutes)

V0.8 G1 (D173): the controller's in-memory live ring of the node's
heartbeat samples (one per ~2 s, the last ``live_ring_size`` of *this*
process) - nothing is read from or written to PostgreSQL. Oldest first.
``age_s`` is measured on the controller's monotonic clock. Empty after a
controller restart until the node reports again; V0.9 replaces the source
(durable telemetry) behind the same shape.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `node_id` | path | string | yes | maxLength 32 |
| `window` | query | integer | no | Seconds back from now (the ring holds about 5 minutes). (minimum 10, maximum 300, default `300`) |

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | Successful Response | `application/json` [NodeMetrics](#schema-nodemetrics) |
| 400 | Invalid input (`invalid_input`) | `application/json` [ErrorEnvelope](#schema-errorenvelope) |
| 401 | No, or no longer a valid, credential (`unauthorized`) | `application/json` [ErrorEnvelope](#schema-errorenvelope) |
| 403 | Not allowed: admin only, CSRF, foreign origin (`unauthorized`) | `application/json` [ErrorEnvelope](#schema-errorenvelope) |
| 404 | Not found - also another user's object (`not_found`) | `application/json` [ErrorEnvelope](#schema-errorenvelope) |
| 409 | Conflict (`conflict`, `no_feasible_plan`) | `application/json` [ErrorEnvelope](#schema-errorenvelope) |
| 422 | Invalid parameters (`invalid_input`) | `application/json` [ErrorEnvelope](#schema-errorenvelope) |

### `GET /v1/clock`

The controller's wall clock (for an NTP-style offset estimate)

V0.9 G0 (D213): the controller's ``time.time()`` when it answers, so a
client can estimate the offset between its clock and the controller's from
round trips (``meshforge.common.clock_offset``: offset ± RTT/2) before it
compares a controller timestamp (an event's ``recv_at``, a transition's
``at``) with its own clock. Authenticated like every route; reads nothing.
``Cache-Control: no-store``: a cached answer would silently ruin the
estimate (fix round 1, DEFECT-6). The time source is the app's
``FabricView.wall_clock`` (V0.9 G1, D226 item 0.4).

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | Successful Response | `application/json` [ServerClock](#schema-serverclock) |
| 400 | Invalid input (`invalid_input`) | `application/json` [ErrorEnvelope](#schema-errorenvelope) |
| 401 | No, or no longer a valid, credential (`unauthorized`) | `application/json` [ErrorEnvelope](#schema-errorenvelope) |
| 403 | Not allowed: admin only, CSRF, foreign origin (`unauthorized`) | `application/json` [ErrorEnvelope](#schema-errorenvelope) |
| 404 | Not found - also another user's object (`not_found`) | `application/json` [ErrorEnvelope](#schema-errorenvelope) |
| 409 | Conflict (`conflict`, `no_feasible_plan`) | `application/json` [ErrorEnvelope](#schema-errorenvelope) |
| 422 | Invalid parameters (`invalid_input`) | `application/json` [ErrorEnvelope](#schema-errorenvelope) |
| 429 | Rate limited; see Retry-After (`resource_busy`) | `application/json` [ErrorEnvelope](#schema-errorenvelope) |
| 503 | A dependency (the database) is unavailable; retry (`network_error`) | `application/json` [ErrorEnvelope](#schema-errorenvelope) |

### `GET /v1/bench/campaigns/{campaign_id}/labels`

Per-group labels: best configuration, tie, insufficient or pending (admin)

Labels from the campaign's run records (docs/TELEMETRY.md "Labels"):
the one row filter (ok, self-check ok, no ``bench_role``), the latest
attempt per (config, repetition), then the median-CI rule. Nothing is
stored; the same records give the same answer (and the same Parquet
bytes, D222). More label rows than ``[controller.telemetry]
export_max_rows`` -> 413.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `campaign_id` | path | string | yes | maxLength 40 |
| `format` | query | enum: `json`, `parquet` | no | json (default) or parquet. (default `json`) |

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|

<a id="schema-evalrequestin"></a>

### EvalRequestIn

``POST /v1/planner/eval-reports`` (admin): start an evaluation.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `allow_leak` | boolean | no | Debugging only: use the live calibration instead of held-out refits; every verdict is stamped 'leaked'. (default `False`) |
| `background` | boolean (nullable) | no | Must be true (V0.15 G6b, D378): the evaluation runs in the background; the answer is 202 {report_id} and GET /v1/planner/eval-reports/{report_id} reports its progress. A request without it (a client from before the change, which expects the report in the answer) is refused with 400 eval_requires_background. |
| `campaign_ids` | array of string | yes | The benchmark campaigns to evaluate (their labelled groups). (minItems 1, maxItems 20) |
| `holdout` | string (nullable) | no | Evaluate only this workload family (held out of the calibration refit). |

| `agent_version_status` | enum: `same`, `behind`, `unsupported` (nullable) | no | V0.17 G5 (Q37), against this controller's version: `same` minor, `behind` (one minor older - still accepted, upgrade soon) or `unsupported` (refused with version_unsupported). Null = no version. |
| `cache` | object of [CacheCount](#schema-cachecount) | no | V0.5 D101: what the node reported it caches, per kind (blob, tree, env, image): item count and bytes. Empty until its first snapshot. |
| `certificate` | [NodeCertificate](#schema-nodecertificate) (nullable) | no | V0.7 G2: the certificate issued at the node's latest enrolment (`meshforge-agent join`); null = never enrolled. Not enforced on the session port before V0.7 G3. |
| `clock` | [NodeClock](#schema-nodeclock) (nullable) | no | V0.9 G1 (D213): the node's wall clock minus the controller's, from Ping/Pong round trips over a recent window (live session, else the most recent session's last estimate); null = never measured. |
| `connected` | boolean | yes | - |
| `cpu_percent` | number (nullable) | no | - |
| `display_name` | string | no | V0.17 G3: the name the laptop's owner gave it in the agent's local console; empty = none, show the hostname. (default ``) |

| `gpus` | array of [GpuUsage](#schema-gpuusage) | no | default `[]` |
| `hardware` | object | no | The ``Hello.hardware`` summary exactly as the node sent it (proto field names; 64-bit values are JSON strings). The agent's richer local facts - per-probe status, duration, reason - are deliberately not on the wire: run `meshforge-agent hardware show` on that laptop (D13). |
| `hostname` | string | yes | - |
| `last_seen_at` | [Utc](#schema-utc) | yes | - |
| `last_session_id` | string (nullable) | no | - |
| `node_id` | string | yes | - |
| `not_enforced` | array of string (nullable) | no | V0.7 G6: the owner caps no runtime limit enforces on this node (``<field>:<why>``, from its live session's owner policy); null = offline or an agent from before V0.7 G5. |
| `os` | string | yes | - |
| `owner_policy` | object (nullable) | no | V0.7 G5 (D142): the owner policy of the node's live session (null = offline, or an agent from before V0.7 G5). ``not_enforced`` lists the owner caps no runtime limit enforces on that node (``<field>:<why>``); ``allowed_users`` is shown as a count only. |
| `peer_address` | string (nullable) | no | - |
| `peer_endpoint` | string (nullable) | no | V0.5 D99: host:port of the node's peer blob server, as accepted from its live session's Hello (null = offline, no server, or refused). |

<a id="schema-transferout"></a>

### TransferOut

One transfer_event row (V0.5 G5, D93): ``source`` is ``cache`` (hits:
``units`` blobs / ``bytes`` already cached, ``duration_ms`` = the tree's
whole staging), ``controller`` or a peer's node id (bytes received, request
time, units won, ``dropped`` = why it was dropped).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bytes` | integer | yes | - |
| `dropped` | string (nullable) | no | - |
| `duration_ms` | integer | yes | - |
| `failures` | integer | yes | - |
| `resumed_chunks` | integer | no | default `0` |
| `source` | string | yes | - |
| `tree_id` | string | yes | - |
| `units` | integer | yes | - |
